title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 157 (Effect of mixture, without bailor’s consent, when the goods cannot be separated)

content.overview: Section 157 provides that if the bailee, without the consent of the bailor, mixes the goods of the bailor with his own goods in such a manner that it is impossible to separate the goods bailed from the other goods and deliver them back, the bailor is entitled to be compensated by the bailee for the loss of the goods.
content.glance: Where non-consensual mixture makes separation impossible, the bailor is entitled to compensation from the bailee for the loss of the goods.
content.study: If the bailee, without the consent of the bailor, mixes the goods of the bailor with his own goods, in such a manner that it is impossible to separate the goods bailed from the other goods and deliver them back, the bailor is entitled to be compensated by the bailee for the loss of the goods. Current-law framing: impossibility of separation converts the bailee’s act into a conversion-like liability for the full value of the bailor’s goods.

examples.title: Inseparable mixture
examples.body: Bailee mixes the bailor’s oil with his own without consent so that separation is impossible. Bailor is entitled to compensation for the loss of the goods under Section 157.

hypotheticals.question: Bailee mixes the goods without consent in a way that makes separation impossible. What is the bailor’s right?
hypotheticals.analysis: Under Section 157 the bailor is entitled to be compensated by the bailee for the loss of the goods.

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 157 provides that if the bailee mixes the bailor’s goods with his own without consent in such a manner that it is impossible to separate the goods bailed from the other goods and deliver them back, the bailor is entitled to be compensated by the bailee for the loss of the goods. This is the counterpart to Section 156 (separable case) and Section 155 (consensual mixture).
examples: Inseparable mixing of liquids without consent — compensation for the loss of the goods.
distinctions: Section 157 applies where separation is impossible; Section 156 applies where separation is possible.
problemApplication: Conclude that the bailor is entitled to compensation for the loss of the goods.
